title: M. Coding-domain filter study
description: Purpose: measure whether the 57-term coding-domain lexicon override should apply to the ML sentiment backends, not just VADER. Re-run tuning + held-out gold sets for vader, transformer-sst2, and transformer (go_emotions-mapped) in two configurations each (with/without a text-level filter variant), on a dedicated synthetic probe set of ordinary coding phrases plus genuinely negative same-word phrases. Done when: all six backend/config combinations reported (probe split, per-set accuracy, confusion matrices), a keep/adjust/remove recommendation implemented per-backend, tests and docs updated. Aggregate numbers only; no message text.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Epic complete. Outcome: per-backend coding filter (on for VADER, off for the transformer family, overridable via --sentiment-coding-filter on|off|auto / config sentimentCodingFilter), backed by the six-config study on both gold sets plus a 24-probe synthetic set. Headline numbers: vader+filter tuning/heldout/combined 1.000/0.462/0.767; vader-raw 0.735/0.423/0.600; goemotions identical 0.971/0.731/0.867 with and without the filter, but the filter converts a genuine-frustration probe to neu and another to pos, so it is removed from the transformer default; sst2 unaffected on gold (0.676/0.346/0.533). Docs and tests updated; suite green (197 suites / 1617 passed).
